summary.headline: Rikhav Securities H1 FY27 consolidated PAT fell to INR13.60 crores on total income of INR869.07 crores, with weak markets and higher costs squeezing margins.
summary.overview: Management described H1 FY27 as a difficult period for Indian equities and broking, citing West Asia conflict, FPI selling, and the April STT hike on derivatives that moderated F&O volumes. Consolidated total income was INR869.07 crores, EBITDA INR24.47 crores, PAT INR13.60 crores and EPS INR3.55, with trading volume above INR73,000 crores across equity, F&O and commodities. Management said it is shifting capital toward brokerage, institutional broking, algo-trading and margin funding, and is starting ETF market making and an advisory vertical (INR3.15 crores). Institutional broking contributed only about INR0.5 crore of brokerage in H1, so most income still comes from the legacy retail and trading business.

financial_highlights.metric: Trading volume handled in H1 (equity, F&O, commodity)

segments.name: Equity broking / retail and HNI clients
segments.commentary: Management says 99% of clients have continued to trade, and brokerage revenue has increased. No segment-level split was given.

segments.name: Institutional broking
segments.commentary: Early stage: about INR0.5 crore brokerage in H1, with about INR1.5 crores expected in next six months and INR3-4 crores targeted for next year. About 15 institutions empanelled including LIC and GIC.

segments.name: Proprietary trading / algo and arbitrage
segments.commentary: Algo-driven arbitrage and delta hedging with VaR-based risk system; majority of funds moved to algo-trading, described as safer. No figures disclosed; proprietary vs client income breakup promised later by email.

segments.name: Market making (SME and ETF)
segments.commentary: Established SME market maker on BSE and NSE; ETF market making commenced, with plans to add more AMCs. Revenue not quantified.

segments.name: Margin trading facility (MTF)
segments.commentary: Book about INR15 crores; management targets at least 50% growth to INR25-30 crores next year, with selective lending for credit-risk control.

guidance_outlook: Institutional brokerage target of INR5 crores in one year (revenue) and INR5 crores brokerage per year within two years; a later answer cited INR10 crores institutional brokerage within two years.
Existing business growth of 20-25% a year; institutional revenue INR3-4 crores next year, growing 20-25%.
MTF book to grow at least 50% to INR25-30 crores next year, conditional on market conditions.
Operating margin pressure expected to persist given higher costs; management expects markets to stabilise and improve in H2 but gave no specific figure.
Capital raise considered around March-April 2027, dependent on market improvement; digital marketing to start after March 2027.
capex_capacity: Technology capex is mainly servers for institutional and ETF market-making clients, plus colocation at NSE and BSE for lower latency.
Point-to-point networking lines from offices to NSE and BSE trading locations.
Hardware costs up 30-40% due to AI-driven demand, though purchases continue at reasonable rates.
Employee and software costs expected to rise 10-15% due to new labour laws and salary increases.
Expansion into UP, Punjab and Rajasthan has just started, beyond Maharashtra and Gujarat; franchise expansion kept selective.
Client API access planned within about three months (next quarter).
demand_pricing: Operating margin fell because expenses rose while income was flat: higher financial costs from SEBI rule changes, new IT systems, higher STT on F&O, and employee cost increases.
Management said the arbitrage disparity persists despite higher F&O taxes and that it is pursuing options-based permutations.
Digital onboarding is live; daily active app users about 10,000, with more than 18,000 logins.
Differentiation claimed as personalised dealer service and API-based customisation.

qa_highlights.question: Strategy to expand the institutional client base over the next two to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: LIC and GIC are empanelled and SBI Group is the next target; 12-15 smaller institutions are planned each year. Institutional business is expected to be net-surplus from next year, with INR5 crores revenue targeted within a year and INR5 crores brokerage within two years.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for capital raising to support institutional, ETF, MTF growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Capital augmentation was planned for March or April 2027, conditional on market recovery. Liquidity is described as adequate today, with more capital to be raised when MTF demand or market activity rises.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of the drop in operating margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Income was flat while costs rose: higher financing costs from SEBI changes, new IT systems, higher F&O STT, and salary increases from new labour laws. Proportionate revenue growth has lagged because the market is weak.

qa_highlights.question: Capex and technology investment over two to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Spending is on servers, NSE and BSE colocation, and P2P networking to support institutional and ETF market-making clients. Hardware costs are up 30-40%, and software and employee costs are expected to rise 10-15%. No total capex figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: MTF book size, growth and credit-risk management?
qa_highlights.answer: MTF book is about INR15 crores, with a target of at least 50% growth to INR25-30 crores next year. Growth is deliberately selective, and client-wise scrip exposure limits are used for risk control. No funding-cost figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Share of H1 income from recurring fee-based business?
qa_highlights.answer: All H1 income came from the legacy business; institutional broking produced about INR50 lakhs. Management expects about INR1.5 crores in the next six months and INR3 crores or more next year.

risks_watch: Margin compression: EBITDA of INR24.47 crores on INR869 crores of income is a thin margin, and costs are rising faster than income.
F&O volume and arbitrage spreads are exposed to the STT hike; management gave no quantified impact.
MTF credit risk and funding cost, with no disclosed NPA or cost-of-funds data.
Institutional and ETF market-making targets are ambitious against H1 brokerage of about INR0.5 crore.
Franchise and compliance risk, and the possible capital raise timing (March-April 2027) tied to market recovery.
Breakup of proprietary vs client-driven income was not given on the call and was promised by email.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term institutional and algo growth, but cautious and often vague on near-term numbers. Management deferred several financial breakdowns (proprietary vs client income, cost split, advertising spend) and gave only partial answers on capital and risk.
key_quotes: Institutional broking is a key growth level for us.
We believe this approach will make our earnings steadier over time irrespective of short-term market movements.
The operating margins is decreased because the income, remains same but the expenses has increased.
That credit risk we are managing very well, so for that credit risk only we are not expanding, in a faster way, we are doing very selective MTF.

adds.what: Expansion into UP, Punjab and Rajasthan (new geographic branch/franchise footprint, selective)

growth.why: Management guides 20-25% annual growth from the existing business, plus MTF book growth of at least 50% to INR25-30 crores and institutional revenue of INR3-4 crores next year; backing is partial (server capex, new UP/Punjab/Rajasthan footprint, institutional empanelment of about 15 institutions) with no quantified capacity or order book, and margin pressure is expected to persist.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA of INR24.47 crores on INR869.07 crores income in H1 FY27, with costs rising while income was flat; employee and software costs expected up 10-15% and hardware up 30-40%, and management expects margin pressure to persist.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Server purchases and NSE/BSE colocation plus P2P lines are under way for institutional and ETF market-making clients, and UP/Punjab/Rajasthan expansion has just started, though no quantified capacity was given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides 20-25% annual growth from the existing business and expects markets to stabilise in H2, but H1 total income was flat and F&O volumes were moderated by the April STT hike; traded volume was above INR73,000 crores in H1.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capital augmentation is planned for March or April 2027, conditional on market recovery, but no total capex figure was given and utilisation was not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management was cautious and vague on near-term numbers, with H1 PAT down to INR13.60 crores and institutional brokerage at only about INR0.5 crore against targets of INR1.5 crores in six months and INR3-4 crores next year.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Institutional and ETF market-making targets look ambitious against H1 institutional brokerage of about INR0.5 crore, and the MTF target of 50%+ growth is conditional on market conditions.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Client API access is planned within about three months, ETF market making has started with more AMCs planned, and the advisory vertical (INR3.15 crores) is new.

rows.label: Institutional broking ramp (LIC, GIC, SBI Group)
rows.why: About 15 institutions empanelled and 12-15 smaller institutions planned each year, with ~INR1.5 crores expected in the next six months and INR3-4 crores targeted next year, from only INR0.5 crore in H1.

rows.label: MTF book growth to INR25-30 crores
rows.why: Book is about INR15 crores with a target of at least 50% growth next year, but growth is deliberately selective and conditional on market conditions, with no funding-cost data given.

rows.label: Capital raise around March-April 2027
rows.why: Management plans capital augmentation in March or April 2027, conditional on market recovery, to support institutional, ETF and MTF growth.

tone.note: Management was confident on long-term institutional, algo and ETF growth but cautious and vague on near-term numbers, deferring the proprietary/client income split, cost breakdown and advertising spend; analysts pushed on margin compression, cost drivers and capital-raise timing.
